From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@omnihealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Extended log retention for upcoming audit

Hi Irene,

We have an external audit scheduled in late Jan and our security team is asking whether Redwood can preserve API request logs and auth/event traces for 180 days rather than the default window. The SIG questionnaire flagged a gap because some of our investigator playbooks require 6 months of access to request-level logs.

Specific asks:
- Can you confirm whether Redwood can retain request logs and KV/cache access logs for 180 days for a single customer account?
- What evidence do you provide for preservation (Audit log exports, signed amendment, chain-of-custody notes)?
- Any cost or operational impact we should budget for (storage, retrieval SLAs)?

I've attached our audit checklist for reference. Procurement may also want a short amendment to the contract. Can you loop in security and legal?

Thanks,
Samantha Lee
Senior Information Security Manager
OmniHealth

Attachment: OmniHealth-Audit-Checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Extended log retention for upcoming audit

Hi Samantha — thanks for the note and the checklist.

Short answer: we can offer a customer-specific preservation amendment, but it requires a scoped agreement (what exact logs, retention window, export cadence) and acceptance of an addendum due to the operational cost and controls required.

Next steps I propose:
1) Ben (security) and Laura (legal) — can you weigh in on technical feasibility and the standard amendment template?
2) Samantha — can you confirm which of the following you need preserved for 180 days: API request logs (ingress/egress headers + timestamps), authentication events, KV/cache access logs, and model inference metadata?
3) If feasible, we'll produce a short amendment and a preliminary cost estimate. I attached a quick cost worksheet we use to size storage and retention operational effort.

We should be able to turn the amendment around ~5 business days after scope confirmation.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: retention-cost-estimate.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Request: Extended log retention for upcoming audit

Hi all,

Thanks for pulling this together. A few clarifying items from the security/compliance side:

1) Scope: We can include API request logs (request/response metadata without full payloads), auth events, and a subset of inference metadata (model id, token counts, latency). We cannot routinely retain full request payloads that contain customer-provided PII unless the customer signs a separate data processing amendment and we verify compliance with our minimization policy.

2) Controls: Preserved logs would be stored in an encrypted archival bucket, access-controlled, with an immutable retention flag. Access would be granted only to named OmniHealth contacts plus Redwood security for incident response; all retrievals are logged with an approval workflow.

3) Evidence: For SOC 2 / SIG purposes we can provide:
   - a signed preservation addendum (template attached)
   - a CSV export of retained log indices and a time-stamped retrieval log
   - an attestation letter from Redwood security outlining controls and retention window

4) Operational impact/cost: 180d retention for request-level indices increases storage and retention admin. The attached draft amendment includes a variable monthly surcharge (or one-time commit) depending on volume; we can bake this into a contract amendment.

If OmniHealth confirms the exact log types to preserve, I'll prepare the amendment and a short attestation document. Laura — happy to coordinate the legal language in the template I attached.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: retention-amendment-template.docx (document stub)

Irene/Ben — thanks for the fast turnaround and the detail.

Confirmed scope: API request metadata (no request bodies), authentication events, and model inference metadata (model id + latency + token counts). We do not need KV/cache internal indices.

Procurement is prepared to review a short amendment and any monthly surcharge; please include estimated monthly cost and lead time in the draft. We will need the signed amendment in place before the audit kickoff (week of 2027-01-25).

Also: would you be able to provide a short attestation letter we can include in the audit pack (one page, controls summary + retention window)? That would be ideal.

Thanks — looping in procurement at procurement@omnihealth.com for contracting.
